predecessors.name: Somavamshi dynasty
predecessors.text: Dakshina Kosala (Chhattisgarh), Kalinga-raja's Tummana near Bilaspur

successors.name: Maratha Empire
successors.text: the Ratanpur kingdom, annexed by its suzerain Nagpur

ledger.x: c. 1000: Kalinga-raja sets up the Ratnapura branch at Tummana. "The Ratnapura branch was established by Kalinga-raja around 1000 CE." He conquered Dakshina Kosala from the Somavamshi dynasty; the branch were "an offshoot of the Kalachuris of Tripuri" and vassals of them for many years.
1740: "the general of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom, Bhaskar Pant invaded the kingdom."
1740: "The Ratanpur kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom in 1740."
1758: "The kingdom survived until 1758, when its last ruler Mohan Singh died" and the state was annexed by its suzerain, the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom.

wars.name: Jajalla-deva I against the Chindaka Nagas
wars.outcome: "Jajalla-deva I defeated the Chindaka Naga king Somesvara and took him prisoner"; his release followed his mother's intervention; the same year southern Kosala was annexed from the Telugu Choda governors.

wars.name: Ratna-deva II against the Eastern Ganga
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II repulsed an invasion by Anantavarman Chodaganga; the page describes "a long conflict for the control of the Trikalinga and Kosala regions".

wars.name: Ratnapura independence from Tripuri
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II "officially declared independence from the Kalachuris of Tripuri"; Gayakarna's army sent against him "was defeated".

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Ratanpur kingdom
wars.outcome: Bhaskar Pant invaded and the kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom; annexed in 1758 on the death of Mohan Singh.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on the page; Dakshina Kosala (Bilaspur) and southern Kosala are the only places it names, and 1226-1739 has no information at all.
